title: kitchen.settings.update
description: Kitchen configuration (one singleton row per hub): KDS display + order behaviour (merge of ADR-0014). The generic settings form of the shell sends the WHOLE snapshot (upsert), so every property is `required` — and therefore every property MUST carry a `default` equal to its column DEFAULT in `migrations/postgres/001_init.sql`. Without it, a hub whose singleton row does not exist yet (every new hub, since the row is born from this form) starts the form empty and its first save is a 422 nobody can get past (kitchen#41). Pinned by `tests/settings_defaults_match_the_column.contract.test.py`. Every property here is READ by code that runs, pinned by `tests/every_setting_moves_something.contract.test.py`: ten controls that reached nothing were retired in kitchen#48 (`auto_accept_orders`, `items_per_page`, `auto_refresh_seconds`, `sound_on_new_order`, `sound_on_rush`, `auto_bump_enabled`, `auto_bump_delay_seconds`, `auto_print_tickets`, `use_rounds`, `auto_fire_on_round`). Their COLUMNS survive with their DEFAULT — dropping one needs a `kind: contract` migration no module can publish — so a hub that had saved values keeps them; the form simply stops offering a switch that moved nothing.
